coverage_policy_notes: Targets are research goals, not quotas. Under-covered groups require a documented coverage_exception; titles are never reclassified to fill a quota.
notes: Political orientation and radicality require attributed provenance; FSC does not convert editorial endorsements or party preference into an unsourced political classification.
Party press is an independent dimension and is not a political group.
Reach and circulation are metadata, never inclusion thresholds.
English- and Spanish-language print publications are in scope.
research_notes: American Renaissance is excluded from the active-print candidate pool because its publisher states the monthly print magazine ended in January 2012.
Workers World remains an active print candidate: its publisher offers a monthly mailed 12-page print paper and current 2026 PDF issues.
Jacobin remains an active print candidate: its publisher offers a four-issue annual Print + Digital subscription in 2026.
La Opinión remains an active Spanish-language print candidate: its publisher describes it as the most-read Spanish-language print newspaper in the United States.

Puerto Rico legacy titles El Nuevo Día and Primera Hora require time-sensitive handling because their publishers announced print cessation in September 2026; they must not be treated as stable active-print candidates.

Current 2026 third-party classifications support New York Times, Washington Post and USA Today as lean-left; Wall Street Journal news as center; Reason and Newsweek as center; Washington Examiner, National Review and Epoch Times as lean-right; New York Post news as right. These are candidate-level provenance assertions, not FSC judgments.

ADL identifies The Barnes Review and American Free Press as right-wing extremist publications carrying Holocaust-denial content; SPLC separately documents The Barnes Review as extremist. Both still offer active print subscriptions in 2026.
US right and radical-right print form groups remain sparse; coverage exceptions are preferable to moving lean-right/conservative publications solely to satisfy targets.
Washington Examiner is an active weekly print magazine in 2026; its 2026 media kit reports 44 issues and 45,000 copies weekly.
The Nation, In These Times, Current Affairs, Jacobin, Dissent and National Review all have verified active 2026 print editions/subscriptions.
Current Affairs publishes six print issues per year in 2026 and describes itself as a left magazine; In These Times publishes 10 print issues per year in 2026.
The Atlantic is rated Left by AllSides as of 2026; The Nation is rated Left. These classifications are stored as external assertions rather than FSC labels.
Los Angeles Times is rated Lean Left by AllSides and remains a candidate for left-liberal newspaper coverage.
Washington Times is rated Lean Right by AllSides and remains a conservative/lean-right candidate.
Catalyst was removed from the immediate candidate pool pending stronger verification of an active 2026 US print subscription/product.
